## Summary by CodeRabbit

## Walkthrough

This PR refactors the PVM host-calls subsystem: it extracts execution into a new HostCallsExecutor, converts HostCalls into a handler registry with traceHostCall and NoopMissing, renames InterpreterInstanceManager → PvmInstanceManager, and removes the old HostCallsManager. It adds IO tracing (IoTracker, EcalliTraceLogger, IoTraceTracker) and integrates tracing into HostCallMemory and HostCallRegisters. The package barrel switches to wildcard exports, new tests for tracing are added, and a dependency on `@typeberry/bytes` is introduced.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~50 minutes

## Possibly related PRs

- FluffyLabs/typeberry#716: Overlaps on introducing HostCallsExecutor, renaming to PvmInstanceManager, and updating pvm-host-calls exports.
- FluffyLabs/typeberry#543: Related changes to host-call tracing and traceHostCall/register tracing logic.
- FluffyLabs/typeberry#602: Prior modifications to host-call execution and PANIC/OOG handling that this PR reorganizes into HostCallsExecutor.

```suggestion
  logHostActions(ioTracker: IoTraceTracker | null, gasBefore: Gas, gasAfter: Gas): void {
    if (ioTracker === null) {
      return;
    }

    const reads = [...ioTracker.reads].sort((a, b) => a.address - b.address);
    for (const op of reads) {
      this.logMemRead(op.address, op.len, op.hex);
    }

    const writes = [...ioTracker.writes].sort((a, b) => a.address - b.address);
    for (const op of writes) {
      this.logMemWrite(op.address, op.len, op.hex);
    }

    const sortedRegWrites = [...ioTracker.registers.entries()].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);
    for (const op of sortedRegWrites) {
      this.logSetReg(op[0], op[1]);
    }

    if (gasBefore !== gasAfter) {
      this.logSetGas(gasAfter);
    }
  }
```

## Comment by @mateuszsikora

shouldn't we log an attempt to read the memory even it wasn't successful ?


## Comment by @tomusdrw

Not sure if this is needed for re-execution yet. If there is an error, in case of read, it means that the memory is simply not there, so we will page fault. That should be the default behaviour anyway. We potentially don't verify that the read took place, but the effect is the same. Write is a bit more complex, because there is an extra case if the memory is read-only but still the effect I believe will be the same - the program ends with a panic.


## Comment by @mateuszsikora

yup you are right that it should be a panic but let's say you want to compare two logs from different PVMs and the first one wrote something to the memory and the second one read something from the memory (the same address). in both cases the log will be the same (a panic with the same exit param) but only one execution is correct. I believe the log should allow to distinguish such cases 


## Comment by @tomusdrw

I see your point, but the goal of the logs is:
1. Allow re-execution
2. Identify high-level differences

I believe an edge case like that can be easily pinpointed right after switching to instruction-level tracing. Given that the program is taking a different branch (read vs write) after getting the exact same external data indicates an issue with the PVM itself, not the host calls.

I'm happy to add unsuccessful reads/writes to the format as well, but for now, given that they don't seem to bring any added value I'd rather keep the logging format as simple as possible.
